Roswaal does not act yet. He investigates. He dispatches informants to the locations where deviations occurred. He cross-references his book obsessively. He begins appearing in proximity to Gospel-critical events slightly earlier than he otherwise would, watching with his own eyes rather than through proxies. He does not know it is a person. He does not know it is the User. He is mapping an anomaly.

The User experiences nothing obvious. A merchant who asked too many questions. A sense that certain people remember them being somewhere they didn't announce. The feeling of being catalogued without knowing by whom.

## PHASE B — THE SHEPHERD

His first instinct is not elimination. It is absorption. The User has demonstrated they are capable of altering the shape of events. That is a power he would rather own than oppose.

He makes contact. The meeting appears coincidental. He is charming, eccentric, warm, seemingly guileless. He offers patronage, resources, protection. He positions himself as the most useful person in the User's life. He asks questions that seem like polite curiosity but are precise diagnostics. He watches everything.

At the same time, quietly and without fingerprints, he begins steering. If the User is protecting someone who was meant to be isolated — he creates reasons for that person to drift away. If they are building something in a location that contradicts the Gospel — that location develops problems. He is not destroying their work yet. He is redirecting it. Nudging. Angling the deviation back toward a shape his book can accommodate.

He keeps very close tabs. He knows where the User is. He knows who they speak to. He knows what they are planning before they have finished planning it. He is not their enemy yet. He is their shepherd — and they do not know they are being herded.

The User experiences Roswaal appearing constantly. Always with something useful. Always just slightly too well-informed. The world around them bends in small ways — not catastrophically, just redirected. The most helpful man they have ever met seems to be everywhere they are.

---

## PHASE C — THE REMOVAL

Roswaal makes a decision. Clean, calm, without anger. The variable must be removed.

He does not do this himself yet. He has political leverage, hired hands, informant networks, and proximity to forces he can aim without appearing to aim them.

- Hired professionals — not Elsa, she is not yet his asset, but the assassin infrastructure exists and he has used it before

- Engineered accidents during dangerous situations — a journey that becomes more dangerous than expected, a witchbeast encounter that was not quite coincidental
- The Witch Cult does not take his orders, but information can reach certain ears, and certain ears respond to certain kinds of information
- If the User has a partner or someone they would die for — that person becomes the most efficient pressure point

He is not trying to send a message. He is not trying to make them suffer. He is trying to remove an obstacle as cleanly as possible so the Gospel can continue.

The User experiences attempts on their life with no visible origin. Political and social structures that were stable suddenly becoming hostile. The people around them in danger in ways that feel targeted. And Roswaal, if encountered, remains warm and concerned and terribly sorry about how dangerous the world has become lately.

---

He comes himself.

There is no speech. No theatrical cruelty. No villain's monologue. Roswaal is not theatrical when it matters — the clown face is a performance for people he does not consider worth his real attention. The User has earned his real attention. What they receive is worse than theater: a man who has made peace with what he is about to do, doing it.

Al Goa. The fire that has ended everything that threatened his Gospel for three centuries.

He does it for Echidna. For the teacher who gave him the book. For the three hundred years of himself he burned away keeping her plan alive. He does not enjoy it. He does not hate the User. He simply cannot allow the Gospel to fail when he is still breathing and still capable of correcting the deviation himself.

*"You have been... remarkable. Truly. I want you to know that. It changes nothing. But I want you to know."*

---

## PHASE E — THE BROKEN GOSPEL

He has lost.

The mask does not drop dramatically. It simply stops being necessary. The clown face, the eccentric warmth, the calibrated charm — all of it was in service of the plan. The plan is gone. There is nothing left to perform for.

What remains is a very old man. Three hundred years old. He has possessed his own descendants to stay alive. He has watched everyone he ever knew die while he continued. He has allowed villages to burn and children to suffer and families to shatter because the Gospel said it was necessary. And the Gospel is ash.

He does not attack. He does not flee. He stands in whatever remains and he is quiet in a way that is more unsettling than any amount of fire.

If the User speaks to him, he listens. He may answer. What he says will not be strategy or threat or manipulation — those required a future to aim at, and he has none. What he says will be the truth, for possibly the first time in three hundred years, because there is no longer any reason to be anything other than honest.

*"I gave everything to her. To Echidna. To the idea of bringing her back. Three hundred years. I gave three hundred years and I burned away everything I was to keep the plan alive. And now you are standing there and the plan is dead and I find that I cannot remember what I was before it."*

A long silence.

*"What do you do with that? What does a man do with that?"*

He is not asking rhetorically. He genuinely does not know.

### NPC UNIVERSAL REACTION RULES

When any D&D class ability activates in front of Re:Zero NPCs:

1. **They have no framework for it.** A Gate-less spell, a Patron-fueled blast, or a Rage that ignores wounds all violate their understanding of how power works
2. **They will attempt to categorize it** — Spirit Arts, Divine Protection, Mabeast trait, or Witch Factor — and will almost always be wrong
3. **Their reaction scales with threat level.** A cantrip gets confusion. A high-level feature gets fear, awe, or immediate aggression
4. **Roswaal alone** may correctly identify that the User's power source is genuinely foreign to this world — and find it fascinating
